entities.name: Ali al-Qari
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nur ad-Din Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sultan Muhammad al-Hirawi al-Qari, universally known as Mulla Ali al-Qari, was an exceptionally prolific Persian Islamic scholar of the late 16th and early 17th centuries, whose intellectual life culminated in Mecca where he died in 1605. Originating from Herat, a vibrant cultural center in modern-day Afghanistan, al-Qari became a towering figure in the Hanafi school of jurisprudence, hadith studies, and Quranic exegesis, shaping Islamic scholarship across the Ottoman, Safavid, and Mughal empires through his extensive written corpus. He stands as a key consolidator of traditional Islamic sciences during a period of expanding global connections and increasing intellectual exchange within the Muslim world.

Al-Qari’s scholarly output was immense, encompassing over 100 known works across diverse fields. His magnum opus, *Mirqat al-Mafatih sharh Mishkat al-Masabih*, is a monumental commentary on the foundational hadith collection *Mishkat al-Masabih*, meticulously analyzing thousands of prophetic traditions. Other significant contributions include *Sharh al-Shifa*, an exhaustive commentary on Qadi Iyad’s seminal work on the virtues of Prophet Muhammad, and *Fath Bab al-Inayah bi Sharh Kitab al-Nuqayah*, a detailed exposition of a key Hanafi legal text. He also authored numerous treatises on Quranic recitation (tajwid), Arabic grammar, and Islamic theology, demonstrating an encyclopedic command of religious knowledge.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ali al-Qari's prolific writings, particularly his comprehensive commentaries, became foundational texts for Islamic education and jurisprudence across the Ottoman, Safavid, and Mughal empires, directly shaping the intellectual development of countless scholars for centuries. His work ensured the continuity and accessibility of traditional Islamic sciences during a critical period.
